channel.title: Mitchel Pawirodinomo
channel.description: Writing on infrastructure, Go tooling and side projects.

item.title: Reviving Dozer, a menu bar hider nobody maintained
item.description: Dozer hides menu bar icons, has about 8,700 stars and hasn't been updated in years. It also crashed whenever the screen locked. I forked it, fixed the crash, moved it to a Swift package that builds without Xcode, and ran into what macOS 26 does to menu bar items.

item.title: Building ColimaUI, a native macOS app for Colima
item.description: I dropped Docker Desktop for Colima and missed the dashboard. So I built one: a SwiftUI app that lays out stacks, containers, logs and disk use like Docker Desktop, as a thin window over the CLI tools I already had.

item.title: Building Onchain Stocks, a portfolio view for tokenized stocks on Base
item.description: A static, read-only viewer for Coinbase's 40 stock tokens on Base, with no scam tokens and a half-second load on slow phones.

item.title: Exposing local services with Cloudflare Tunnel
item.description: Put a local service on a real domain with cloudflared: no port forwarding, no dynamic DNS, and the catches to know first.

item.title: Ditching Docker Desktop for Colima and Portainer
item.description: Colima gives me the Docker daemon, Portainer the dashboard, and my compose files didn't notice the difference.

item.title: Building CryptoWatcher: the macOS Stocks widget, in my terminal
item.description: A weekend Go project: macOS Stocks-style cards with Braille line charts and one watchlist for crypto and stocks.

item.title: Building Cashly, my self-hosted finance tracker
item.description: I stopped using budget apps and built a Go daemon that reads bank alert emails and tracks fiat and crypto in one place.

item.title: Why I built bcron: a scheduler I can actually see
item.description: Scheduled jobs that fail silently, with output nobody kept. bcron is a small Go scheduler with a background daemon, SQLite history and a terminal UI.

item.title: Scraping 8 Surinamese banks without losing my mind
item.description: No Surinamese bank has a rates API, so I scrape them: parsers that survive redesigns, stale data on purpose, and a PWA.
